name: Wormwood
grown_as: Wormwood (absinthe), a hardy perennial grown for its silver leaves. Drawn as the plain species; 'Lambrook Silver' is similar. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: An upright, bushy clump 60 to 120 cm high, many ribbed, silvery stems from a woody base, branching above into leafy flower sprays.

leaf.type: Simple but deeply cut: two or three times divided, feather-like
leaf.outline: Broadly oval to triangular overall, 5 to 10 cm long on the lower leaves, cut almost to the midrib into many narrow, oblong segments 2 to 4 mm wide; upper leaves smaller and less cut, the top ones narrow and whole
leaf.veins: Hidden under the hairs; only the midribs show
leaf.surface: Covered in fine silky hairs on both sides, a little whiter beneath
leaf.stalk: Long on the lower leaves, short or none on the upper

flower.form: Tiny round, button-like heads, with no petals
flower.petals: None to see: each head is a ball of tiny tube flowers
flower.centre: The whole head is the centre
flower.behind: A cup of grey, hairy bracts
flower.carried: Many heads, nodding on short stalks, along the branches of a loose, leafy, upright pyramid-shaped spray

fruit: Tiny brown seeds with no fluff; the heads dry grey-brown.
winter: Dies back to a woody base, often with a low tuft of silver leaves.

leaf: a leaf deeply cut two or three times into many narrow segments
each segment blunt with a smooth edge
a stalk on the lower leaf
bloom: tiny round yellow heads with no petals
young: a low clump of silvery, deeply cut leaves
growing: an upright bushy clump of silver stems and feathery silver leaves
leaves set singly, not in pairs
flower: tall leafy sprays covered in tiny nodding yellow balls
silver deeply cut leaves below, smaller and less cut above

look_alikes: Mugwort has leaves dark green above and white beneath with pointed lobes, and upright reddish-brown heads on purple stems. Southernwood has thread-fine green segments. Artemisia 'Powis Castle' is finer cut and rarely flowers.
